segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ ״יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ נְדָרִים, אֲבָל אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְפִירִין״, יָפֵר. ״יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְפִירִין, אֲבָל אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁזֶּה נֶדֶר״, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: לֹא יָפֵר, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: יָפֵר.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If a man’s wife or daughter took a vow and he failed to nullify the vow on the day he heard it, but afterward he said: «I know that there are vows, but I don’t know that there are those who» can «nullify» them, i.e., he was unaware of the possibility of nullifying vows, «he can nullify» the vow of his wife or his daughter on the day he learned that he can nullify vows. If, however, he said: «I know there are those who» can «nullify» vows, «but» I refrained from nullifying the vow that I heard because «I do not know that this» is considered «a vow, Rabbi Meir says he cannot nullify» the vow at this point, «but the Rabbis say» that even in this case «he can nullify» the vow on the day that he learned of his mistake.
